newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen leader says willing meet Eritrean president.
newsitem.headline: Yemen leader says willing meet Eritrean president.

text.p: Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh said on Sunday he has accepted a French offer to arrange a meeting between him and Eritrean President Isayas Afewerki on a territorial dispute between the two countries.
"We are in continued direct and indirect contacts (with Eritrea) through French envoy Francis Gutman," Saleh told reporters in the capital Sanaa.
"(Gutman) is arranging a meeting soon with Afewerki...And we have agreed to the meeting," he added.
He said no date has been set for the meeting.
Yemen and Eritrea signed an accord in Paris in October to set up a court to resolve their territorial dispute over the Lesser Hanish island, one of several islands claimed by both states.

Arab Yemen and African Eritrea, facing each other across the Red Sea, fought briefly last December over the potentially oil and gas-rich islands, which lie near tanker routes at the Red Sea's southern entrance.

The conflict worsened last August when Yemen threatened to take military action if mediation failed to defuse a crisis triggered by dispatch of Eritrean troops to Lesser Hanish. Eritrea later said it had withdrawn its forces.
"The meeting...will be good for the normalisation of relations and a return to the situation we had before (the crisis erupted)," Saleh said.
